entries.test: Published research available by August 2022 documenting widely recognized reliability, toxicity, and other problems in the language technology underlying PaLM-SayCan.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give 'problematic' a concrete reading.
Explicitly qualified by 'likely.'
The bull-in-a-china-shop comparison is figurative characterization.
Recommends expanding the risk list.
Predicts possible damage, not a firm outcome.

entries.test: Public evaluations of contemporary language models interpreting user requests would establish whether they regularly misunderstand intended meanings.
entries.note: The plain reading concerns reliable interpretation of requests, not direct access to private thoughts.
Misunderstandings are predicted firmly, but resulting mayhem is only a possibility. The combined claim retains that qualification.
There is no shared threshold for an idea being 'compelling' across the many alignment problems.
The antecedent is the absence of a compelling solution idea, not simply unsolved problems. 'Superficial statistical mimics' and 'rich cognitive models' lack shared operational criteria here.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and deployments establishing reliable general-purpose household performance by robots built on the described language systems would test the predicted failure.
entries.note: 'Cannot succeed' makes the idiomatic warning more absolute. Context supplies reliable domestic robotics as the relevant success criterion.
The architecture is checkable, but the full characterization supplies no shared test for 'superficial and incorrigible.'

entries.test: Contemporaneous public forecasts and expectations compared with documented autonomous-driving reliability and deployment progress through August 2022 would test the claimed underestimate.
entries.note: Public expectations and missed deployment timelines provide a plain comparative test.

entries.test: Industry technical publications and public statements over time would show whether edge cases dominated remaining reliability problems and when the industry recognized that.
entries.note: 'Recently' refers to the few years preceding August 2022.

entries.test: Public robotic-system evaluations on unusual situations and previously learned edge cases would test whether these systems share the described generalization and forgetting problems.
entries.note: The source denies grounds for exemption and refers to both edge-case variety and forgetting. The normalization asserts exemption is false while narrowing the problems to infinite edge cases.

entries.test: Formal-verification literature available by August 2022 would show whether established methods used in the cited engineered systems had a demonstrated application to language-model-driven behavior.
entries.note: The source specifies the kinds of verification used in microprocessors, USB drivers, and aircraft. The normalization broadens this to formal verification generally.
'Hard to see how' expresses uncertainty about a route to safety; 'unlikely' turns that into an outcome-probability assessment. Neither is a firm prediction.

entries.test: Public results showing whether scaling training data alone produces reliable household robots capable of handling unfamiliar situations would test the claim.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies household reliability and learning from limited experience as the relevant problems.

entries.test: Commercial availability records and independent capability demonstrations as of August 2022 would show whether consumers could purchase a robot performing a useful range of intelligent household tasks.
entries.note: The household-assistant context supplies a plain reading of 'decently smart.'

entries.test: Google's published PaLM-SayCan evaluation results would establish its best-case task success rate under the limited action options.

entries.note: The proposed performance relationship is explicitly qualified by 'likely.'

entries.test: Google's action-level PaLM-SayCan evaluation results would establish whether any tested actions had zero correct executions.
entries.note: The numerical observation is checkable; the appended adequacy judgment is evaluative.
Judges an acceptable level of performance rather than reporting a measured result.

entries.test: Product announcements, sales records, and independent deployment reports through October 2026 would show whether PaLM-SayCan became a practical household product in the years after the post.
entries.note: The rhetorical question is immediately answered with a firm dismissal. The following paragraph clarifies the near-term horizon as several years.

entries.test: Public deployment records and independent reliability evaluations through October 2026 would show whether conversational robots reliably performing a range of everyday household chores materialized within several years of August 2022.
entries.note: 'Should not hold our breath' conveys a firm negative expectation, but the normalization removes its idiomatic qualification. The several-year horizon has elapsed on an ordinary reading.
